Japan Central Alps
by Ninja Tours

Sunday 10/4

Arrive Tokyo

On the road

Land at Haneda and get to the Minami-Senju area, where Rushcorp is based. The airport limousine bus stops outside the Asakusa View Hotel, which is one stop from Minami-Senju on the Tsukuba Express — the easiest door-to-door route with luggage.

Worth stopping for

  • Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori — five minutes' walk from most Asakusa hotels, and best after dark when the day crowds have gone.
  • Kappabashi kitchenware street, if you want knives to ship home.
  • Hoppy-dori for a first-night izakaya dinner.

Watch for

Sort your IDP, licence and passport into one pocket tonight. Rushcorp will want all three in the morning.

Monday 10/5

Tokyo → Kusatsu

Tokyo200 kmKusatsu
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

Pickup at Rushcorp, then north out of the city on the Kan-etsu Expressway to Shibukawa. From there the character changes completely: R353 and R145 run west up the Agatsuma valley, climbing steadily through gorge country before the final zigzag up to Kusatsu at 1,200 m. Deliberately easy for a first day — expressway for the dull part, one good climb at the end.

Worth stopping for

  • Agatsuma Gorge — a narrow rock canyon along R145, signposted from the road, with short walking paths if you want to stretch.
  • Yanba Dam — completed in 2020 after decades of controversy; the new lake and the viewing platforms are worth ten minutes.
  • Kusatsu Yubatake — the wooden cooling channels in the centre of town, floodlit at night, and the source that feeds Naraya's baths.
  • Sainokawara open-air bath — a large rotenburo at the top of the park, five minutes' walk up from the Yubatake.
  • Netsu-no-yu — the yumomi water-stirring performance, several shows daily.

Watch for

Ride time is short but you will be jet-lagged. Aim to be off the road by mid-afternoon.

Lodging

Naraya

One of Kusatsu's long-established inns, right by the Yubatake and fed directly from it. Rated 4.3 from 800+ reviews. Kaiseki dinner, tatami rooms, and staff who handle English well. Reviewers note the bath is on the small side with no outdoor section — the town's public rotenburo make up for it.

www.kusatsu-naraya.co.jp ↗

Tuesday 10/6

Kusatsu → Matsunoyama

Kusatsu120 kmMatsunoyama
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

The best road of the trip, and it comes early. R292 — the Shiga-Kusatsu Kogen Route — climbs out of Kusatsu past the Shirane crater and tops out at Shibu Pass, 2,172 m, the highest point on any national highway in Japan. Above the treeline it is bare volcanic rock and long sightlines. Over the top you drop into Shiga Kogen, then the Oku-Shiga Kogen Road threads north through beech forest to Kijimadaira. From Iiyama, R117 follows the Chikuma River southwest into the Niigata hills.

Worth stopping for

  • Shibu Pass and Yokoteyama — pull off at the summit car park for the view back over the Shirane massif.
  • Shiga Kogen ponds — Kido-ike and Maruike sit right beside the road and are at peak colour in early October.
  • Nozawa Onsen — a short detour off R117; thirteen free public bathhouses scattered through the village.
  • Matsunoyama's terraced rice fields and the Bijin-bayashi beech grove, a few minutes from the inn.
  • Kyororo, the rust-steel nature museum in the woods above the onsen.

Watch for

R292 has a seasonal night closure and marked no-stopping zones near the Shirane crater because of volcanic gas. Ride it in the morning and check the day's status before you set off.

Lodging

Hinanoyado Chitose

Rated 4.4 from 500+ reviews. Matsunoyama is counted among Japan's three great medicinal hot springs, and the water here is dense, saline and very hot. One indoor bath and two outdoor, kaiseki built on local produce, and the Uonuma rice is a genuine highlight. Secluded, wooded, and quiet.

chitose.tv ↗

Wednesday 10/7

Matsunoyama → Sekikawa

Matsunoyama210 kmSekikawa
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

The longest day so far and the least famous, which is part of its appeal. North through Tokamachi and the Uonuma basin on quiet prefectural roads, across the Niigata plain, then up into the Arakawa valley on R113 — the old Yonezawa highway — to Sekikawa. Rice country for most of it, with the harvest just finished and the paddies gold.

Worth stopping for

  • Kiyotsu Gorge Tunnel of Lights — east of Tokamachi; a disused rail tunnel turned into a mirrored viewing installation. A detour, but a memorable one.
  • Echigo-Tsumari art fields — outdoor sculpture scattered through the villages around Tokamachi; you will pass several without trying.
  • Hoshitoge terraced rice fields, best in the early morning when mist sits in the valleys.
  • The Arakawa valley on R113 — a genuinely pretty river road for the last stretch into Sekikawa.

Lodging

Takanosukan

Rated 4.0 from 186 reviews. Reached across a suspension bridge over the Arakawa, with riverside rooms and detached Japanese-style cabins. Dinner is served in-room and reviewers consistently describe the volume of food as enormous. Little English spoken, but staff are used to guests with translation apps.

www.takanosukan.com ↗

Thursday 10/8

Sekikawa → Nikaho

Sekikawa170 kmNikaho
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

Out to the Sea of Japan and north along R7 for most of the day, with the water on your left the whole way. The middle section is the Sasagawa Nagare — around eleven kilometres of sea stacks, arches and clear green water — then the road passes Nezugaseki into Yamagata, runs behind Tsuruoka and Sakata, and finishes at Kisakata under the western flank of Mt. Chokai.

Worth stopping for

  • Sasagawa Nagare — pull off at any of the several viewpoints; the rock formations have individual names and the water is unusually clear.
  • Atsumi Onsen — a small hot spring town just off the highway, good for lunch and a foot bath.
  • Mt. Haguro — a detour inland from Tsuruoka to a 600-year-old five-storey pagoda in a cedar grove. Worth the hour if you have it.
  • Sakata — the Sankyo rice warehouses with their row of zelkova trees, and the Homma Museum garden.
  • Kisakata — Basho came here to see a bay of ninety-nine islands; an 1804 earthquake lifted the seabed and the islands now sit in rice paddies. Odd and rather beautiful.

Watch for

Kisakata is also known for rock oysters — worth asking the inn about if they are still in season.

Lodging

Sannemu Onsen (Sun Nemunoki)

Rated 4.1 from nearly 400 reviews, renovated in 2015. Sulphurous water with cold spring water fed in continuously, a large communal bath and bookable private baths — one with a Finnish sauna. No open-air bath. Reviewers rate the food highly, particularly the rice and the local seafood. A large roadside station and convenience stores are close by.

www.sun-nemunoki.jp ↗

Friday 10/9

Nikaho → Hachimantai

Nikaho160 kmHachimantai
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

Short in distance, big in character. The Chokai Blue Line climbs from near sea level to about 1,150 m at Hokodate in a series of tight switchbacks, with the Sea of Japan below you the whole way up — on a clear morning it is one of the finest roads in Tohoku. Back down, then inland through Yuzawa and Kakunodate, past Lake Tazawa, and over Sengan Pass on R46 into Iwate.

Worth stopping for

  • Chokai Blue Line and the Hokodate viewpoint — go early; cloud builds on the mountain through the day.
  • Kakunodate — the best-preserved samurai district in the north, dark wooden walls and weeping cherries. Twenty minutes' walk end to end.
  • Lake Tazawa — the deepest lake in Japan at 423 m, and a startling cobalt blue. The gilded Tatsuko statue stands in the shallows on the west shore.
  • Nyuto Onsen — up a side road from Tazawa; if you have a spare hour, Tsurunoyu's milky open-air bath is the famous one.

Watch for

The Chokai Blue Line is seasonal and closes for winter. Mid-October should be fine, but confirm before committing to it as your route.

Lodging

Hotel Mori-no-kaze Oshuku

Rated 4.2 from 300+ reviews, at Oshuku Onsen in Shizukuishi with Mt. Iwate behind it. Three linked buildings, large rooms, and options with private in-room onsen. Reviewers say the exterior looks dated but the interiors are well kept, and single out the dining hall and the evening performance. Two minutes from the golf course.

www.morinokaze.com ↗

Saturday 10/10

Golf: Hachimantai Country Club

On the road

No riding. The course is effectively next door to the hotel — under two kilometres — so panniers stay packed and the day is entirely yours.

Worth stopping for

  • Mt. Iwate fills the skyline from most of the course; mid-October should have the surrounding forest in full colour.
  • If you finish early, the Hachimantai Aspite Line is an hour north and makes a superb afternoon out-and-back.
  • Koiwai Farm, twenty minutes east, for the tree-lined approach and soft-serve.

Lodging

Hotel Mori-no-kaze Oshuku (second night)

Same inn as last night — no packing, no check-in, and the baths are waiting when you come off the eighteenth.

www.morinokaze.com ↗

Sunday 10/11

Hachimantai → Naruko

Hachimantai200 kmNaruko
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

South the length of Iwate into Miyagi. If you skipped the Aspite Line yesterday, take it this morning and drop down the far side; otherwise R4 south past Morioka is the fast line. The last stretch into Naruko runs through the Naruko Gorge, which in mid-October is one of the best foliage runs in Tohoku.

Worth stopping for

  • Hachimantai Aspite Line — high, open, and near its foliage peak at this altitude.
  • Morioka — Iwate Park, the Ishiwarizakura cherry tree growing out of a split granite boulder, and jajamen for lunch.
  • Hiraizumi — the UNESCO temple complex; Chuson-ji's gold-leafed Konjikido is the one to see. Adds about an hour.
  • Geibikei Gorge — flat-bottomed boats poled through a limestone canyon, east of Hiraizumi.
  • Naruko Gorge — the Ofukazawa bridge viewpoint is the classic shot. Naruko town is also the home of kokeshi dolls, with workshops open to visitors.

Watch for

Naruko Gorge at peak colour on the Sunday of a long weekend will be busy. Ride it early or late, and expect the gorge car parks to be full in the middle of the day.

Lodging

Naruko Onsen Yumoto Kissho

Rated 4.1 from over 1,000 reviews. Naruko's valley has an unusual number of different spring types, and this is one of the larger properties — public baths, bookable private baths, a yukata selection, buffet breakfast and the free late-night noodles the Dormy group is known for. Reviewers are split on the buildings but consistent that the water is the real thing.

dormy-hotels.com/resort/hotels/kissho ↗

Monday 10/12

Naruko → Kaminoyama

Naruko120 kmKaminoyama
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

The shortest riding day of the trip, and on a national holiday that is exactly right. R47 west along the Mogami valley, then south through Obanazawa to Yamagata and on to Kaminoyama. Gentle roads, and enough spare time to make two or three real stops rather than riding past everything.

Worth stopping for

  • Ginzan Onsen — a short detour north of Obanazawa; Taisho-era wooden inns facing each other across a stream, gas lamps at dusk. The most photographed hot spring street in Japan, and it earns it.
  • Mogami River boat trips — traditional flat boats with a singing boatman, from Furukuchi.
  • Yamadera (Risshaku-ji) — a thousand stone steps up a cliff to a temple among the rocks, where Basho wrote the cicada haiku. Allow ninety minutes.
  • Kaminoyama Castle and the samurai residences below it; there are free foot baths dotted through the town.

Watch for

Holiday Monday is the national return day, so expressways toward Tokyo will be solid. You are travelling the other way on back roads — no problem, but do not be tempted onto the Tohoku Expressway southbound.

Lodging

Koyo (Japanese Inn Koyo / Koyoga)

Rated 4.4 from over 2,200 reviews, which is a very large sample for a ryokan. A big, well-known Kaminoyama inn: rooftop bath with an outdoor section, some rooms with private open-air tubs, and dinners built around Yonezawa beef and Tsuyahime rice. Breakfast is served in a large hall, which a few reviewers find impersonal.

www.koyoga.com ↗

Tuesday 10/13

Kaminoyama → Inawashiro

Kaminoyama130 kmInawashiro
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

South on R13 through Yonezawa, then the day's centrepiece: the Bandai-Azuma Skyline, a high volcanic road that runs along the Azuma range at around 1,600 m past bare sulphur slopes and dwarf pine. It drops down to Fukushima, from where you cut west to Inawashiro under Mt. Bandai.

Worth stopping for

  • Yonezawa — Uesugi Shrine and the castle grounds; and it is the obvious lunch stop if you want the beef at source.
  • Bandai-Azuma Skyline — stop at Jododaira for Azuma-Kofuji, an almost perfectly symmetrical crater you can walk up to the rim of in fifteen minutes.
  • Tsubakuro Valley and the Fudosawa bridge, near the Fukushima end of the Skyline.
  • Goshiki-numa — the five coloured ponds on the Ura-Bandai side, each a different shade from mineral content. A flat 3.6 km walking trail links them.
  • Lake Inawashiro — the fourth largest in Japan, with Mt. Bandai reflected in it on a still morning.

Watch for

Two things to check. The Bandai-Azuma Skyline has a seasonal night closure and volcanic gas restrictions near Jododaira. And the booked inn, Tsukino Akari, is at Aizu Higashiyama Onsen in Aizuwakamatsu — roughly 25 km southwest of Inawashiro, so the real day is closer to 155 km.

Lodging

Tsukino Akari, Aizu Higashiyama Onsen

Rated 3.4 from 132 reviews — the weakest-reviewed stop on the itinerary, and worth a second look before you commit. It runs a deliberately minimal-service model with self-service yakiniku dinner. Reviewers praise the renovated baths and the rice, but several found the food poor and the shared floor toilets dated. Higashiyama itself is an old and pleasant onsen district on the edge of Aizuwakamatsu.

tsuki-no-akari.jp ↗

Wednesday 10/14

Inawashiro → Nikko

Inawashiro200 kmNikko
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

South on R121, the old Aizu-Nishi highway, through thatched-roof country and river gorges to Kinugawa, then west to Nikko and up the Irohazaka switchbacks to Lake Chuzenji. Irohazaka is two one-way roads with forty-eight hairpins between them, each signed with a character from the Japanese syllabary.

Worth stopping for

  • Ouchi-juku — a preserved Edo post town of thatched houses on an unpaved street. Touristed, but genuinely striking, and the negi-soba eaten with a spring onion instead of chopsticks is a local ritual.
  • Tonohetsuri — eroded cliff formations above the Okawa river, reached by a footbridge.
  • Yunokami Onsen station — the only thatched railway station in Japan, with a foot bath on the platform.
  • Nikko Toshogu — the shogun's mausoleum complex; allow two hours if you stop, and it is easier before the climb than after.
  • Kegon Falls and the Chuzenji lakeshore torii, both a few minutes from the inn.

Watch for

Irohazaka and Lake Chuzenji are at peak foliage in mid-October, and the uphill road jams from mid-morning. Aim to be climbing before 10:00.

Lodging

Hotel Hana-an, Lake Chuzenji

Rated 4.2 from nearly 500 reviews, on the Chuzenji lakefront looking across to the great torii. Public onsen plus rooms with private baths, and reviewers repeatedly single out the view and the kaiseki dinner. English is spoken. Kegon Falls and the bus terminal are a few minutes' walk.

www.hana-an.jp ↗

Thursday 10/15

Nikko → Tokyo

Nikko170 kmTokyo
Open this day's route in Google Maps ↗

On the road

Down the Irohazaka descent first thing, then the Nikko-Utsunomiya road onto the Tohoku Expressway and south into the city. Straightforward riding, but it ends with Tokyo traffic and a handover, so build in margin.

Worth stopping for

  • Akechidaira — the ropeway station just below the top of the descent, with the classic view back over the hairpins and Kegon Falls.
  • Shinkyo, the red arched bridge at the entrance to Nikko, if you want one last photograph.
  • Toshogu, if you did not get to it yesterday.
  • Utsunomiya for gyoza — the city is famous for it and it is right on the route.

Watch for

The Irohazaka downhill road jams badly from mid-afternoon through early evening in foliage season. Be off the mountain by mid-morning and the rest of the day is easy.

Lodging

Tokyo — final night

Nothing booked yet. Onyado Nono Asakusa is worth considering: tatami throughout, its own hot spring baths, free evening ramen, and two minutes from the airport limousine stop for the morning flight. Asakusa View Hotel is the other option — bigger rooms and the limousine bus at the door, though a number of reviewers report noise.

Friday 10/16

Depart

On the road

Airport limousine from Asakusa to Haneda, or the Tsukuba Express and Keikyu if you prefer rail.

Booking priority. Hachimantai Country Club for Sat 10/10 — it is an 18-hole course on the Sports Day long weekend, and reviewers report long waits. Then the two Hachimantai nights, then Naruko.

One correction. Tsukino Akari is at Aizu Higashiyama Onsen in Aizuwakamatsu, roughly 25 km past Inawashiro — day 10/13 is nearer 155 km.

Before you ride. Carry the international driving permit, home licence and passport together. Confirm seasonal status for R292, the Chōkai Blue Line and the Bandai-Azuma Skyline — all three have night closures or volcanic gas restrictions. Closure links are on the bikes page.
